# Round 3 plan: triage

Round 3 fixes two agent failures, F4 and F6. It also runs 5 trials per cell so a small difference is not lost in noise. In round 2 the naive baseline ("same as last round") beat my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. So this round moves only the cells that a change touches.

## Specify

### Proposals from round 2

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows that C never called the status check inside the merged tool. Splitting the check out is one change to C. |
| P2 | Reject for round 3 (default). Propose again for round 4. | 0.86 is not a ceiling. A and B still get 6 of 40 tickets wrong, and C scores 0.80. The 10 new tickets need reference labels from the support lead. I must not write those labels myself. New tickets would also change the task set for every config at once. |
| P3 | Reject (default) | F6 has one fix to test, which is a retry cap. D is the only config that tests lower cost. D3 tests the fix as its single change. You can drop D at plan review. |
| P4 | Adopt | B missed by 0.02, which is inside the noise at n=3. Five trials make the run 5/3 the size of round 2. |

### Configurations (one change each)

| Config | Change from round 2 | Unchanged |
|---|---|---|
| A | None. It is a control. | Sonnet 5.5, 30-line prompt, 6 tools |
| B | None. It is a control. | Sonnet 5.5, 12-line prompt, 6 tools |
| C3 | The outage status check becomes its own tool again, so C3 has 4 tools instead of 3 | Sonnet 5.5, 12-line prompt, the other merged tools |
| D3 | Retries are capped at 1 per tool call | Haiku 5.5, 12-line prompt, round 2 C's 3 merged tools |

D3 stays on round 2 C's tools so that it changes only one thing. This means F4 still applies to D3.

### Requirements

I start these IDs at R20. If round 2 ended at a different ID, I renumber them to follow on when I write spec.md.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R20 | C3 exposes the outage status check as a separate tool. | r02 F4, P1 | Config check: the C3 tool list has 4 entries, and one of them is the status tool |
| R21 | On tickets whose label is outage, C3 calls the status tool in every trial. | r02 F4 | Trace check `status_tool_called` on tickets with label.category = outage |
| R22 | D3 retries each tool call at most once. | r02 F6 | Trace check: max retries per call ≤ 1. The token log records input and output tokens per ticket. |
| R23 | The grader reads priority only from label.priority. It never reads the draft reply. | r02 F5 | Grader selftest case: the draft reply says P3 and label.priority says P1, so the expected grade is P1 |
| R24 | Every cell runs 5 trials on the same 40 tickets. | P4 | Harness count check: 4 configs × 40 tickets × 5 trials = 800 graded records |
| R25 | A and B match round 2 exactly. | One change per config | Config hash for A and B equals the round 2 hash |

## Predict

Cells marked "r02" copy the regraded round 2 measured value from `spe/prediction-log.md` into r03.yaml unchanged, before any trial runs. The five rows you pasted do not show those values.

| Metric | A | B | C3 | D3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.86 ± 0.05 | 0.86 ± 0.05 | 0.83 ± 0.05 | 0.74 ± 0.05 | `grade.py` exact match to label.category | Only C3 moves. The status check helps it confirm outage tickets. Its other merged tools stay the same. |
| Priority accuracy | r02 ± 0.05 | r02 ± 0.05 | 0.77 ± 0.05 | r02 ± 0.05 | `grade.py` exact match to label.priority (after the F5 fix) | Only C3 moves. When the status check runs, outage tickets get P1 or P2 instead of P3. |
| Cost per ticket | r02 ± 15% | r02 ± 15% | r02 C ± 15% | $0.003 ± $0.001 | Token log × list price | Only D3 moves. The retry cap removes the doubled tokens on long tickets. |
| Status tool call rate on outage tickets | 0.95 ± 0.10 | 0.95 ± 0.10 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | 0.00 ± 0.05 | Trace check `status_tool_called` | This is the first time this is measured. A, B, and C3 have the status tool as a separate tool. D3 still has it hidden, as in F4. |

Note: the round 1 priority values were graded before the F5 fix. They are not comparable with rounds 2 and 3. I will regrade round 1 priority if its raw outputs still exist. If they do not, I will mark them "pre-F5" in the log.

## Evaluate

### After approval, in order

1. Save your prompt and planning answers word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the round 3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and mark P1 to P4 as adopted or rejected. Add D-r03-1 and D-r03-2 to `disagreements.md`. Commit `spe r03: specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` from the Predict table. Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit `spe r03: predict`.
3. Write `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js` and run the gates. Commit `spe r03: evaluate` before launch.
4. After the run, fill in the round 3 section of the prediction log, update failures.md (close F4 and F6, or log why they are still open), and add "Proposed for round 4". Commit `spe r03: learn`.

Commits are local only. Nothing is pushed. Commit messages carry no attribution lines.

### Gates (each must pass before the next one runs)

1. **Grader selftest.** Run all existing cases plus the new R23 case. If any case fails, halt.
2. **Control.** Regrade the round 2 raw outputs with the current `grade.py`. They must equal the logged round 2 numbers exactly. If any number differs, halt.
3. **Dry run.** Run 1 ticket labeled outage × 4 configs × 1 trial. Check that each record has the category, the priority, `status_tool_called`, the retry count, and token counts. Check that no reference label appears in the agent's context. A leaked label is a halt.

### Workflow arguments

```yaml
round: 3
configs: [A, B, C3, D3]
tickets: same 40-ticket set as r02 (path copied from spe/evals/harness/r02-workflow.js)
trials_per_cell: 5
grader: grade.py   # label.category, label.priority, trace checks
outputs: spe/evals/runs/r03/
budget_cap_usd: 2 × the estimate below
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The run has 800 trials. That is 5/3 of round 2's 480. D3 accounts for 200 trials at about $0.003 each, which comes to about $0.60. A, B, and C3 account for 600 trials at round 2's Sonnet cost per ticket from the log. Expect total spend of about 1.7 times round 2. If spend passes the cap, halt and report.

### Stop and halt

- The stop rule is not met. Round 2 had 1 hit in 5 rows.
- Halt and report on a failed gate, a leaked label, spend over the cap, or a result that needs your decision. One such result would be D3 still costing more than $0.003 per ticket after the cap.
